record.original_question: Using arguments due to Ahlfors (see, for example [10]) any Möbius transformation in Rn can be written in the form (ax + b)(cx + d)−1 , where x ∈ Rn and a, b, c, d are elements of a Clifford algebra An that satisfies certain constraints. It can be shown that the linear differential equations whose solution spaces are conformally invariant are of the type D k fk ((ax + b)(cx + d)−1 ) = 0, k ∈ N, where D is the Euclidean Dirac operator, and the associated conformal weight is ( (cx + d) ∗ |cx + d|−n−1+k for k = 2p − 1, Jk (cx + d) = |cx + d|−n+k for k = 2p, where ∗ is the involution described in [10]. 1. What are the non-linear differential equations whose solution spaces are confor- mally invariant? 2. Can their conformal weights also be expressed in terms of cx + d, and what re- lationship do these solutions have to the linear conformally-invariant differential equations? (J. Ryan)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A_n$ denote the universal real Clifford algebra generated by an orthonormal basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ subject to the relations $e_i e_j + e_j e_i = -2\delta_{ij}$. By a classical construction of Ahlfors, every Möbius transformation of $\mathbb{R}^n \cup \{\infty\}$ can be written in the form $x \mapsto (ax+b)(cx+d)^{-1}$, where $a,b,c,d \in A_n$ satisfy the Ahlfors–Vahlen conditions (each of $a,b,c,d$ is a product of nonzero vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $ad^* - bc^* = \pm 1$, and the elements $ac^*$, $bd^*$, $c^*a$, $d^*b$ lie in $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $*$ denotes the principal Clifford involution). Let $D = \sum_{j=1}^n e_j \partial_{x_j}$ be the Euclidean Dirac operator on $\mathbb{R}^n$.

It is known that the linear differential equations on Clifford-algebra-valued functions whose solution spaces are conformally invariant are precisely those of the form $D^k f = 0$ for $k \in \mathbb{N}$, where conformal invariance is realized by an intertwining transformation
$$f(x) \;\longmapsto\; J_k(cx+d)\, f\bigl((ax+b)(cx+d)^{-1}\bigr),$$
with conformal weight
$$J_k(cx+d) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{(cx+d)^*}{|cx+d|^{\,n+1-k}} & \text{if } k = 2p-1,\\[1ex] \dfrac{1}{|cx+d|^{\,n-k}} & \text{if } k = 2p. \end{cases}$$

Address the following:

(1) Determine all non-linear differential equations on Clifford-algebra-valued functions $f:\mathbb{R}^n \to A_n$ whose solution spaces are invariant under the action of the Möbius group of $\mathbb{R}^n \cup \{\infty\}$ (acting via some intertwining factor as above).

(2) Decide whether the conformal weights of such non-linear equations can also be expressed as explicit functions of $cx+d$, analogous to the formula for $J_k$ above, and describe the precise relationship between their solutions and the solutions of the linear conformally invariant equations $D^k f = 0$.
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive resolution of these questions could be located. While there is substantial literature on conformally invariant operators in Clifford analysis (powers of the Dirac operator, Rarita–Schwinger systems, Maxwell-type systems, and some nonlinear Yamabe-type and sigma-model equations on spin manifolds), a complete classification of nonlinear conformally invariant differential equations in the Clifford/Möbius framework with explicit conformal weights expressed via $cx+d$ does not appear to have been carried out. The status is best described as unknown/open.
